Euljiro 3-ga is a bit away from the crowded draft beer bars, so the street is a bit quiet, but the atmosphere inside the pub is hot. At the sundae restaurant across from the pub, Koreans and foreigners are standing in line waiting for their turn. If I have time, I should check out this sundae restaurant.

When you enter a pub and order a draft beer, you are given fried corn and some snacks, which are standard snacks at a draft beer restaurant. The idea is to enjoy it with a glass of hops until the snack you ordered is ready. When it was time to finish the glass of hops, fruit snacks including pine mushrooms and dried persimmons were served.

Pine mushrooms are an improved species of pine mushrooms and shiitake mushrooms and are also called ‘pine mushrooms.’ The mushroom cap resembles a shiitake mushroom, and the mushroom stalk resembles a pine mushroom, with a pine mushroom flavor. When you dip pine mushrooms in oil and chew them, the scent of pine mushrooms fills your mouth.

Songhwa mushrooms alone make a great beer snack. After snacking on dried persimmons and fruit and chatting with friends I had met for a long time, I felt refreshed and after adding a few 500cc glasses, I got up. It was a very pleasant day.

“A quiet Korean lounge where you can forget the noise of the city”

Atmosphere: Just by going down the stairs in the middle of Jonggak Street of Youth, a different world unfolds. The interior, which reinterprets the atmosphere of a hanok in a modern way, is truly cozy and luxurious.

Food & Cocktails: Signature cocktails ‘Harvest’ and ‘Reunion’ are unique and deep flavors that can only be tasted here. From the welcome tea and medicine and service to the dried persimmon dessert, it is the ultimate in neatness.

Service: I felt treated well as each menu item was explained kindly. I highly recommend it as a place for dates or small gatherings where you want to have a quiet conversation.

reviews.author: jinwoo Chae
reviews.text: Hanuk, a cocktail bar near Jonggak Station, was a place that blended Korean sensibility with a subtle atmosphere. There is no parking lot in the building, but it is a short walk from a nearby public parking lot, so the visit itself was not difficult. The moment I went down to the basement entrance, a welcome scent spread and I immediately felt like I was in a different space. Inside, the lighting was low and Hanok-style objects were placed here and there, creating a naturally calm atmosphere. From the bar seat, you can see the cocktail making process right in front of you, so ordering a drink felt like an experience in itself. The menu was organized like a small book, so it was fun to choose a cocktail featuring traditional ingredients. As soon as I sat down, the sujeonggwa and yakgwa served to me were subtly sweet and made me feel like my nerves were gently melting away. ‘Harvest’ had a harmonious combination of citron scent and milk foam, and was a taste that even first-time drinkers could enjoy comfortably, while ‘Jaehoe’ was a style that was easy to drink after a meal, with the scent of Schisandra chinensis and vetiver remaining for a long time. The light appetizer went well with the cocktail and blended naturally into the overall composition. Thanks to the quiet and balanced atmosphere, it was a satisfying time to the point that I thought it would be a good idea to visit with foreigners as well as for dates or gatherings with acquaintances.

reviews.author: wooden bird
reviews.text:
I visited Hanuk, a cocktail bar located near Jonggak Station.
Because it is a space with a Hanok motif, the atmosphere is really nice, and the interior with its cornerstones and pillars was impressive. The bar table and private sitting area are separated, making it especially great for a date.

reviews.text:
Myeongdong Night Market, located in the center of Seoul, is one of the representative nighttime attractions that domestic and foreign tourists must visit. Myeong-dong is already well-known as a mecca for shopping, fashion, and beauty, but at night, the street transforms into a night market with a completely different charm. Here, you can enjoy a variety of street food, food, souvenirs, and traditional crafts all in one place, making it a steadily popular nighttime tourist destination in Seoul.

In particular, the biggest advantage of Myeongdong Night Market is accessibility. Transportation is convenient as it is close to Myeongdong Station on Subway Line 4, and it is also close to major tourist attractions such as Namsan Tower, Seoul City Hall, and Euljiro, so it is naturally included in the travel route. It is famous among foreign tourists as a place to experience traditional Korean street food. Representative menu items include tteokbokki, hotteok, fried chicken, hot dogs, grilled skewers, tornado potatoes, and octopus skewers, and there are a variety of food booths lined up every night, so you can enjoy the diverse flavors of Seoul at once.

In addition, Myeongdong Night Market is more than just a place to eat, it is also a shopping night market where you can enjoy live performances, street busking, and purchase unique handicrafts, accessories, and traditional souvenirs. Especially on weekends and holidays, there is a lot of floating population, so you can feel a lively atmosphere, and it is also a popular spot for social media photos such as Instagram and YouTube.

Myeongdong Night Market's operating hours are usually from 5 p.m. to late at night, but may vary depending on the season and day of the week. It is a good idea to check the times in advance before visiting. In addition, foreign language guidance is well provided, so tourists who speak English, Chinese, or Japanese can use it conveniently.

If you are planning a trip to Seoul, Myeongdong Night Market is more than just a place to eat, it is a place where you can experience Korean night culture, street scenes that combine tradition and modernity, and a global atmosphere enjoyed by multinational tourists.

editorial_summary: This bell tower was used to tell the time in the 1300s and features an elaborate exterior. Today, the bell-ringing ceremony is held daily.

reviews.author: Roy L.
reviews.text:
Bosingak was a bell tower that told the time in the center of Hanyang during the Joseon Dynasty.
• Paru: At around 4 a.m., the bell was rung 33 times to lift curfew and the four main gates were opened. (Number 33 symbolizes the 33 heavens of Buddhism and prays for the peace of the nation)
• Recognition: Around 10 p.m., the bell was rung 28 times to signal curfew and the gate was closed. (Number 28 symbolizes the 28 constellations in the sky)
Originally, it was just called 'Bell Tower', but in 1895, King Gojong personally wrote and gave it a plaque reading Bosingak, and it received its current name. It symbolizes trust among the five virtues of Confucianism (benevolence, righteousness, propriety, knowledge, and faith), which means maintaining trust in the center of Hanyang City.
Every year at midnight on January 1st, the 'New Year's Eve Bell' event is held, and the bell currently hanging is a replica.
The current bell is a new bell made with public donations in 1985, and the original Bosingak bell (Treasure No. 2) made during the reign of King Sejo is currently being moved to the National Museum of Korea for preservation due to the risk of cracking.
